name: War memorial

layers.essential_history: [[c:The memorial was unveiled on Armistice Day 1920 by Colonel Proby of Elton. It's a sandstone pillar topped with a stone ball, a laurel garland, a coronet and a small cross. Names from the Second World War were added later.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:It became a Grade II listed building in 2015, partly because it stands so close to the Grade I listed church.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:There's no story page here. The memorial is a place of remembrance, so we've kept it out of the mystery.]]

directions_to_next: [[c:Head north-west for about 40 metres to St Mary's church. The church is right beside the memorial. Keep to the pavements and paths, and look from the road only.]]
notes: Keep the war memorial and individual graves out of the fictional mystery.
